It says here that somebody, a masked person, came to you first and that he was followed by a doctor, and they told you that you were not a problem but that the problem are your encaptured brethren who had about a 1 million 6 hundred thousand Deutschmarks on them and that they were tortured by Croats.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the part that refers to the 9th of May, where it says that a man came to you, he spoke about those encaptured Arabs. He said that they were not soldiers, that they were mostly humanitarians and journalists and there were only three soldiers and that he was afraid that what had happened might pose problems for the future activities of Merhamet and the Islamic centre, the two humanitarian organisations, one of them religious? Is it true that this person told you that and did you write that in your report?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever you can find in this report is what I could remember best, and these are all facts. This is what I was told. I did hear that from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not in a single line of your report, not under any date did you mention the fact that you mentioned here today, when you were talking about kidnapping and linking it with the BH army and the military police of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the special police of the 3rd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have stated what I heard, and I heard that this had been done by a company of the special military police of the 3rd Corps. Whether this was the case or not --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you didn't put it down in your report, and this is my question.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can find it in a different report. Yes, I did write it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the report that you wrote in 1993, you didn't state that fact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe you can't find it in this report. You can find it in another report, however.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please look at the statement that you gave and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. signed and which was recorded on the 13th of October, 1993. On page 1, paragraph 2, you also describe people who kidnapped you wearing masks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 6, you say that one of them shoved a rifle barrel in your back, they spoke in Arabic, and that you recognised the name Totic being mentioned in Arabic?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the kidnapping you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there was very little communication among them. Everything that was said was in Arabic. They had walkie-talkies in the vehicles, and all I could hear was them shouting, "Allah-U-Ekber." There was very little other communication. It was all in Arabic. However, during the act of kidnapping, there was also very -- there was also people acting to be speaking Arabic. They were locals who pretended to speak Arabic, but they couldn't speak it well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on page 2 of this statement given on the 13th of October you describe your departure from the place of kidnapping to the place where you spent the first night after the kidnapping? You say in paragraph 3 - paragraph 3 - "They were very disciplined at first and then they started shouting and singing Arabic songs." You also say that you heard swear words and these were the first words that you heard in Croatian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this statement, you also say that you noticed some people pretending to be foreigners; however, that it was not very well done and that you could recognise them as being locals, rather than foreigners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not in a single line of this statement do you mention anything that you have testified today before this Trial Chamber, which is that somebody during your stay in detention told you that they belonged to the BH army, that the BH army was involved, that it was carried out by the special units of the 3rd Corps. In this statement, no such thing is mentioned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not in my statement, but you can find it in other documents, in other papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, when you gave your statements in 1993, when your memory was still fresh, and when you gave your statement to the highest authorities of the HVO and the police of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, you never mentioned the things that you mentioned before this Trial Chamber today.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, when I spoke to the highest authorities, the suspect was the 7th Muslim Brigade. However, when I was being interrogated and when a statement was being taken from me - and this was all recorded - if there is a will -- these statements that I gave during my detention, all these statements were recorded, and it is true that this person told me that if I should say who had kidnapped me, that I and the closest of my family would be killed. Then I was asked whether I knew who the kidnappers were. I said No, I didn't know. And then they told me the company of the special police of the 3rd Corps. I cannot guarantee that this indeed is true. I know that there were such forces in the Ministry of the Interior Affairs. However, this could not have been done without the knowledge of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So your testimony, that you know, and that one of the kidnappers told you that the kidnapping had been carried out by the special unit of the military police of the 3rd Corps, you didn't hear from any of the kidnappers. You heard that when you gave your statement. You heard it from some other persons who had their doubts at the moment that this was done by the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard it from the kidnappers, that this was done by the company of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you did not mention that in any of the statements that you gave in 1993. You didn't deem it important at the time, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did write that in some of the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, the fact that the BH army, the 7th Muslim, and the 3rd Corps were involved, you started talking about that when -- during your preparation for the testimony in the Kordic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. Your Honours, already in 1993 and 1994 I spoke about that; however, this was not insisted upon, because we were not sure. I cannot say to this very day that this was indeed the unit. We didn't want to judge somebody in advance without proof.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's go back to the part of the testimony that you gave yesterday. What you said yesterday about your information that you had in 1992 and 1993 about the situation in Zenica, this can be found on pages 52 and 53 of the transcript - I'm going to paraphrase - in 1992, you already knew there were foreign troops in Zeljezno Polje, Arnauti, and Mehurici; did you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that you got this information from your intelligence service that you had in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only learned about the foreigners in Bistricka village. That's what my intelligence service told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the 15th of April, 1993, you personally never went to the village of Bistricka, to Zeljezno Polje, or to Arnauti and Mehurici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I subsequently passed through Zeljezno Polje. Before the war, I'd never been there. And I've never been in these villages before, the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up until your kidnapping in the middle of April, 1993, you personally never established contact with the foreign soldiers, the Mujahedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's correct that I never met them and spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the time when you were kidnapped in the middle of April 1993, you never saw any documents from the 3rd Corps or from 3rd Corps brigades which mentioned that foreign soldiers, Mujahedin, were in those brigades or corps. On the contrary, all those to whom you spoke said that they weren't part of the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's correct that all the commanders of the BH army distanced themselves from those people and they said that they weren't part of the BH army -- or rather, they weren't part of the Territorial Defence, which later became the BH army, and that they belonged to the MOS; that is to say, the Muslim Armed Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After your exchange on the 17th of May, 1993, up until the end of 1993 -- or rather, up until the signing of the Washington Agreement at the beginning of 1994, you no longer returned to Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Vitez in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. After the exchange, I was assigned to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So after the 15th of April, you had no personal information or any direct experience about the orders and about the identity of those who implemented certain organisational changes in the army and the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as far as the organisational changes in the 3rd Corps are concerned, in the course of the conflict between the Croats and the Bosniaks I knew very little about that. But it wasn't as if I had no information. I had some relatives and friends in Zenica who held middle ranks, and I heard about a lot of things from them. But at the negotiations in Vakuf, at that time we already started exchanging information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The negotiations in Vakuf were in 1994.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In February, towards the end of February.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified before this Court - and you have repeated this today - that your brigade was only -- was in the process of being founded and it wasn't very well equipped, neither in terms of staff or in terms of weapons.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the brigade was formed on the 18th of February. There were about 1.900 men in it. There was about 55 to 60 per cent of infantry weapons. Not all the soldiers had weapons, not to talk about communications equipment, and so on. But in April, they started forming another brigade. In fact, this brigade was transformed into two.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you also testified - and I'm paraphrasing you to avoid repeating everything - you said you had an intelligence organ within the brigade and that the intelligence organ also filmed part of the investigation conducted in the course of the investigation. Is it true that you had an intelligence organ and that you obtained information from them?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a chief of an intelligence service in each brigade, and I had such a chief too. But the intelligence officer isn't present at on-site investigations. The on-site investigation after my kidnapping was conducted by the Security Services Centre, which consisted of Bosniaks and Croats, and it also consisted of military police. So no one from the brigade could attend. And I saw in the district -- at the district public prosecutor's that there were photographs of the crime scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of that investigation, there were army representatives and civilian police and HVO representatives who were involved in it.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The on-site investigation was carried out by the judge from the district military court and a representative of the district military prosecutor's office was also present. Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that. This is something I read about, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you read about that too.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your first assistant for security in the brigade was Dragan Jonjic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he was already being transferred.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, he was someone who worked in a catering establishment.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had finished a high school for social work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After him, your assistant for security was Jadranko Jandric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, he was a professional soldier. He was a non-commissioned officer in the -- he was a junior officer in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Janko Jandric was an officer in the former JNA, not a non-commissioned officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll now move on to certain other questions that you have also testified about. You testified about them yesterday. When describing your military career, you said that on the 26th of April, 1993, while still in detention, you were appointed to the joint command of the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only found out about that when I had been exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, that is a command that was supposed to be formed on the basis of a joint statement from Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, which they signed on the 25th of April. Franjo Tudjman, the President of the Republic of Croatia, was also present. Is that the command you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Zagreb. Yes. It was signed in Zagreb on the 25th, and that document does exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the document exists in the case that you have already testified in?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've provided it here. It's a public document. It's a political statement. And on the basis of that political statement, Mr. -- issued by Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Mate Boban - and it was also signed by Dr. Franjo Tudjman - the commander at the HVO Main Staff at the time was General Petkovic. He assigned the officers from the HVO who would be in that command, the joint command for the BH and for the Operative Zone of Mostar and for the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that from the very first day, the HVO obstructed the work of the joint command?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, from the very first day, I think that the joint command was obstructed by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that the HVO had various pretexts to reject -- to not appear at the meeting scheduled at the last minute?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Whenever we were summoned to meet, we appeared at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that Mr. Stjepan Siber, who was a representative of the BH army, asked on a number of occasions from the HVO representatives to declare whether they would work in the command or not?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Stjepan Siber did say that. But who was Stjepan Siber at the time? Just a figurehead. The others were those who decided what to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that you attended a meeting on the 28th of June, 1993 in Vitez? UNPROFOR and the EU monitors were present, and on that occasion Mr. Stjepan Siber asked you one more time to declare whether you would be appointing people to the joint command and to declare whether you wanted to participate in that command? Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did attend that meeting. Stjepan Siber did want people to be appointed. But he then wanted to start working in Zenica, where no one could provide any sort of guarantees. And he used various tricks, not Mr. Siber but Kadric. He asked both Mr. Hadzihasanovic and Mr. Blaskic in quite dramatic terms. He addressed both of them in dramatic terms. He asked them to do everything to put an end to the conflict, and Siber also spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that these attempts made by the BH army, to ensure that this joint command functioned, after such obstructions Siber sent complaints to UNPROFOR and the European Community and to the Supreme Command of the army, as well as to the staff in Grude? Is it correct that he sent letters of complaint?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know about any letters of complaints sent by Mr. Siber, but when those meetings of the joint command were held, they were held in the UNPROFOR base in Stara Bila -- while we were still at the meeting, there was an attack, and then there were accusations. We weren't in a position to jointly act. I think the 3rd Corps carried out planned actions, planned attacks to obstruct the cessation of hostilities. We were practically defending ourselves at the time. We didn't have forces to attack anyone. We were just defending our lives.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, since you were never official appointed and you never became a member at the numerous requests of the international community and the requests made by General Siber, the joint command became senseless and after the 28th of June it no longer had any meetings; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the period more or less. There simply weren't any more meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'll now turn -- I'll now go back to another subject, which we've stopped discussing since we started discussing your kidnapping. This was an important issue that you have testified about. A while ago we said - and you confirmed this; although, you also added that there were other armed forces, so that's why I'm asking you again - do you know that on the 8th of April, 1993 the Territorial Defence was declared as the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence on that day.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Territorial Defence, yes. But the HVO was also declared to be such.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to ask the witness to be shown --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. In 1992, not in 1993. So on the 8th of April, 1992 would be the date on which the Territorial Defence was declared.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know it was in 1992. The 20th of April is the HVO day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it would be appropriate now, since I'll be showing the witness a number of documents, perhaps it would be good to have a break and then we can show all these documents to the witness after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we adjourn, you've given us two documents. Do you intend to tender them into evidence? The document that is a statement he made on the 13th of October, he gave the statement to someone who is apparently a member of a security service, Mr. Damjanovic; and another document, he signed all the pages, and it was provided to the authorities. Do you want to tender these documents into evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to tender at least one of the two documents into evidence. Perhaps both. But I'll be suggesting that one of the documents be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. For the moment, you don't know which one. Very well. So how many more documents do you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a total of ten documents. We've provided two so far. But I don't think there'll be much discussion about the documents, so we should be able to deal with it quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Because we'll resume at five to 1.00 but we'll only have 45 minutes then. Will that be sufficient for you to conclude your cross-examination and re-examination, if there's going to be any re-examination, or will we have to continue on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished more than half of my cross-examination. I'll try to conclude my cross-examination, but I can't promise anything. There could be objections. There could be -- we might need decisions to be rendered. So I'm not sure that I'll be able to conclude today. But during the break I will try to ensure that we can conclude with my cross-examination by 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will resume at five to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf -- I'm sorry, the Defence. I'm sorry. The Defence -- I somehow thought you were finished. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Mr. President, I have an answer to your question. We're going to tender only the document dated 13 October. Since the witness confirmed that he did hold this confirmation and that he signed the report, can we please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we please have a number for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be P42 -- sorry, DH42. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH42.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two versions, an English version and a B/C/S version, so we have to have two numbers actually.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the English translation of the document will get the exhibit number DH42/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as regards the questions that I have put so far, I'm going to ask just one more question that I omitted to put to the witness. The witness said that he gave a written statement, if one may call it that, a written document while he was preparing for the Kordic case. We have a copy which we will not tender into evidence. Can this be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, is this the document?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I gave a statement. It is probably that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, we didn't get a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have copies for everybody in the courtroom, or do you just have your copy, a copy for yourself?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do have copies for everybody. But I have only one question. Maybe the witness can put the document on the ELMO. But I believe we can work even without this document because we are going to use this just in order to discredit the witness. It is not going to go for the truthfulness of the contents. Can the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You may give -- maybe give a copy to the Prosecution. Mr. Usher, can you please go and get the copy from Mr. Bourgon and hand it over to Mr. Withopf so that Mr. Withopf can follow the questions according to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, please look at paragraph 44. Is it correct that in the last sentence of that paragraph you say: "Moreover, during the negotiations between Muslims and Croats in Uskoplje, after the signing of the Washington Agreement in March 1994, at the moment of frustration Merdan shouted at me. He raised his voice, and he said that he wished that the Mujahedin had killed me while they held me hostage"? Is this what it says here?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But he told me first, "Why didn't we kill you when we had you," and then this. I had this in my notebook among the notes that I took at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what it says here, what I've just read, is different than what you said on page 35, line 13 of the transcript of today's hearing; is that correct? This is not the same.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the same here; however, I'm telling you that he did tell me what I said earlier, and I have that in my notebook under that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are moving on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the witness to be shown Exhibit DH36.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, this is an order issued by Mr. Mate Boban on 10 April 1992. Tell me, please, did you ever see this order before?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it for the first time. I never saw it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, did you know that Mate Boban, president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, proclaimed the Territorial Defence illegal in the whole of the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that the HVO was also legally established and organised. That's what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So your answer --

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was confirmed by the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina in April 1992. It was recognised that there were two armed formations: The Territorial Defence and the Croatian Defence Council. Those were the two legal military formations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, for the transcript, can you answer my question. Were you aware of this order dated 10th April, issued by Mate Boban, pursuant to which the Territorial Defence was proclaimed an illegal military structure in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, no. I see this order for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You may give this document back to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can the witness be shown another document, DH30 and DH41 ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, were you aware of the fact that in May 1992 the Presidency issued a decree with legal effect on the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina? And this is the first document, the decree with legal effect on the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have never seen this decree before. I was a brigade commander. I never read it. I acted in accordance with the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the shorter document. These are amendments to the decree on armed forces. Is it true, Mr. Totic, that all the armed forces were required to fight those who attacked Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time: The JNA, the Serbian forces? So on the 6th of August, 1993, the decree on armed forces was amended and it was stated then that the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina are the army, the HVO, and other military formations that place themselves under the command of the BH army? Is that what it says in here?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the wording of the decree. Again, I apologise. It was on the 6th of August, 1992, not 1993.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm reading this for the first time. I only know that in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina there were two legal armed forces, two militaries, and they both fought the aggressor, and those were the HVO and the Territorial Defence, which was later on turned into the BH army. I was a member of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Totic, that the Croatian Defence Council never placed itself under the command of the Supreme Staff of the BH army in 1992 and in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Croatian Defence Council -- from my point of view, I was a brigade commander. I don't know what was at the very top. We recognised all the decisions of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina until the moment while a Croatian member was still there, and that was Mr. Boras. He had been elected to that body. Later on I don't know whether the decisions were recognised or not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, these decisions that you're looking at by the armed forces were proposed by Jerko Doko, who was elected in the elections, and the Presidency also had some elected members representing the Croatian people. I don't want to enter any legal discussions with you, but I would like to know whether Croatian Defence Council after the 6th of August was under the command of the Main Staff in Grude?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO was under the command of the Main Staff of the HVO. And the commander at the time was General Milivoje Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we please have the two documents back. I would like to go back to your testimony about the way you joined the HVO and the time you joined it. Is it true, Mr. Totic, that at the beginning of May 1992 in Zenica you were invited to a meeting and that you realised that it was a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the Zenica HDZ, which was a -- the Croatian national party, and that during that meeting the establishment and the organisation of the HVO units in Zenica were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the area of Zenica, but in the area of my native town. And it was not in May. It was towards the end of April. I believe that it was on the 29th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that at that time, in mid-May 1992, you were also invited by the commander of the Territorial Defence, Dzemal Najetovic, also an officer of the former JNA, who also led the JNA, just like you, and he asked you to join his brigade as his deputy, as the deputy commander of the 1st Zenica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It was towards the end of May 1992. He did not invite me. We actually bumped into each other when he and his brigade intimidated people in Croatian villages. That's when he made this offer to me, and I told him that I could only accept that when the Territorial Defence would consist of both peoples. At that time, over 95 per cent of the members of the Territorial Defence were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Totic, for the second time - the first time, when you received the mobilisation call-up papers, and the second time, when you were invited by the commander of the 1st Zenica Brigade - you refused to join the Territorial Defence, which was at the time the legal force of -- armed force of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you appeared in the Municipal Staff of the HVO and you placed yourself at their disposal on the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, I held several conversations with them. And then I joined on the 10th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your first task was to form an HVO battalion in your village, and you were appointed a commander of that battalion; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Already at that time the HVO had already established its presidency as the civilian body of authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, in Zenica there were all the legally elected authorities, which in 1992 and 1993 were still multi-ethnic.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were multi-ethnic. I was not involved in politics.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of July, 1992, you were invited to a meeting of the HVO presidency in Zenica, and you realised that they wanted you to become the commander of the HVO Zenica.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was appointed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter would like the witness to repeat this answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, you -- Your answer has not been recorded. Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was yes, I was appointed. At the proposal of the HVO Zenica, I was appointed to the duty in the Municipal Staff of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, on the following day, after this conversation in the presidency of the Zenica HVO, you met with Colonel Blaskic, the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone; and with Dario Kordic, the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; and Ignac Kostroman, the secretary of the HDZ and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct that on the following day I met with them. But not in Zenica. It was in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I never mentioned Zenica. You may have misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did mention Zenica, in the Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to say that. You were appointed by Tihomir Blaskic, the commander of the staff in Zenica, and gave you your first task to establish the Municipal Staff and to train people for combat activities.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff was already under formation, and it was headed by Mr. Zoran Covic. It had already existed. It had already been established.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, in order for me to ask you some further questions and in order to enable the Trial Chamber and my learned friends to follow, I believe that we can do it in the following way: You are a native of Zenica. Were you aware of the situation in Zenica and in its surroundings? Are you familiar with that area?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now going to ask the usher to show the witness a map of the area, and I will ask the witness to mark certain places on this map, the places that he is familiar with. We have enough copies for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, can you tell us what this map represents? What can you see?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a topographic map, and the scale is 1 to 100.000, and it depicts Zenica. I know 95 per cent of these places. I've been to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, can you please put number "1" next to the centre of the town of Zenica. Can you be given a pencil, please.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, can you mark the places that I'm going to mention. Put a circle around them. First Stranjani, the place where you were born, as far as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then can you please mark Novo Selo -- actually, Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then can you please mark Cajdras.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kozarci.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A place close to Preocica, Lupac.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vjetrenice, please.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kuber as well.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you won't find the name here, but maybe you know where Kaonik is. Can you put a circle around it and can you add in your own hand "Kaonik."

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also mark Lasva.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we can see it better. Again, there is no name here, but if you know, can you please show where Stara Zenica is. Can you mark the area of Stara Zenica.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to put numbers from 1 onwards, mark all these different places, and tell us what the places are, because we want to have it on record. So number 1 will be the centre of Zenica, and so on and so forth. Can I please ask you to do that.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of Zenica; number 2, you asked for Stranjani; number 3, Novo Selo; number 4, Lupac; number 5, Cajdras; number 6, Kozarci; number 7, Vjetrenice; 8, Kuber; 9, Kaonik; 10, Lasva; 11, Stara Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you also mark Radakovo with the following number. And I don't know whether I asked you about Lokvine.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you didn't. Here it is, number 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness has recognised the map as part of a topographic map and he has marked various locations, I would like to ask the witness to sign the map and make a note of the date and we will be tendering this map into evidence. But I will be using this map in order to ask some additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is most likely only a pure technical issue; however, I would like to ask my learned colleague to first ask the questions, since only afterwards the map can be tendered into evidence. So far we don't know for what purpose the witness was asked to mark the different locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's not a problem. After having asked the witness the questions, I can suggest that this map be tendered into evidence. So we don't have to discuss this matter now. Could the witness now be shown an order dated the 24th of October, 1992. This is so I can ask the question -- ask the witness some questions. We have a sufficient number of copies for the Chamber and for our learned colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to say that in the course of its investigations, the Defence found this document in the state archives of the Republic of Croatia, which is where HVO documents are kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, is this your order?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is an order that I issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that under item 2, the 1st Platoon is ordered not to allow the BH army forces along the Zenica -- Vjetrenice-Zenica-Ovanaka road. The 2nd Platoon is to -- is to take action with neighbours to prevent the passage of BH army forces from Lokonet [phoen] to Vjetrenice to Lokvine.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given that the witness has recognised the document as his own and confirmed its contents, I suggest that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I'm sure my learned colleague can explain the relevance of this document prior to tendering it into evidence. The Prosecution, at least so far, fails to see the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What is the purpose of tendering this document into evidence? Is it to prove that he actually held a position and was commander of the forces in the Zenica headquarters? What is the objective of tendering this document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the course of his examination-in-chief, the Prosecution asked the witness about events that took place in Dusina in January and the witness said that the army had carried out an attack against Dusina. The next few documents will be -- that will be shown relates to those allegations in the indictment and will relate to what the witness said in the course of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Again, most likely a pure technical issue. I would suggest the Defence is only allowed to tender this document into evidence once my learned colleague asks the additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have already asked a question concerning the document. The document clearly shows that the witness personally issued an order forbidding the BH army to pass through very important roads. And under item 5 in that document, there is an order for -- to carry out reconnaissance of enemy forces; that is to say, the army. The witness has spoken about the joint army, and so on, but all the questions about the document and its contents are evident from the document itself. The witness confirmed that this was a document that he issued and that he issued these orders to his units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll wait for the additional questions to be put before we take a decision. Please continue with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible, could we immediately mark this document for identification to avoid confusion? Because I will be tendering certain other documents into evidence and you, Your Honours, will decide on whether to admit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's mark the document for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be DH43, marked for identification for the B/C/S version; and DH43/E, marked for identification for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the map is concerned, Mr. Withopf, are there any problems relating to the map at the moment or do you want to express yourself about this matter later?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Again, at least so far, the Prosecution fails to see the relevance of both the map and this document, and I wish to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to the date of the document which is marked for identification with DH43. It's the 24th of October, 1992; whereas, the crime in Dusina was committed on the 26th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will also mark the map for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number will be DH44, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now help me to show the following two documents to the witness, one that is dated the 14th of January, 1993, and one dated the 15th of January, 1993 Could we leave the map before the witness, since he might be using it to answer the questions that I will be asking him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a document which is dated the 14th of January and another document, dated the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that this document dated the 15th of January, 1993 has already been shown to a witness and it has an identification number, DH2/E ID. We have now handed this document out so that everyone could have a copy of the document and so as not to have to look for it among the documents already marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, this document from the police administration, dated the 14th of January, 1993, someone signed it for Chief Valentin Coric. Have you previously seen this document?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've never seen this document before, neither of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please have a look at the second document, dated the 15th of January, which was issued by the HVO Main Staff to all HVO units, and it was signed by the HVO chief, Milivoje Petkovic. Did you receive this order as a brigade commander to which it was forwarded? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not receive this order because the brigade under my command wasn't part of the Main Staff. It was part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. This is the first time I've seen this document. Because I didn't receive documents from the top level.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown a document dated the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as the document DH2, marked for identification, which has already been presented, for technical reasons it should be shown. The document that the registrar has should be shown, not a new copy. So, Mr. Registrar, you will give the usher document DH2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When showing this, Your Honours, we didn't have the English version. Now we have the English translation of the document. And as in the case of the previous document, this document was obtained in the HVO archives, which are in the state archives in Zagreb. The Defence obtained the document in the course of its investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, this document is dated the 16th of January, 1993, 011184/93, signed by Commander Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document, dated the 15th of January, was signed by the chief of staff, Milivoje Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I wanted you to be shown a different document. You have already commented on this first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness another document, dated the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which we don't have. The document dated the 16th of January, we don't have that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness comments on this document, could we mark the document dated the 15th of January for identification, the document signed by Milivoje Petkovic. This is a document that the witness has already seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But this document has already been given a number, DH2/E. Why do you want a new number?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want a new number. I just want this document to be marked for identification. I want the English version to be marked for identification too, because as I have already said, Your Honours, only the B/C/S version was previously marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have a document DH2 in B/C/S, and we have been presented with the English translation. Mr. Registrar, the document dated the 15th of January, 1993, the English translation of that text requires a number, and it has to be marked with an "E."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH2/E, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, this document is 01-184/93 dated the 16th of January, 1993, signed by Commander Tihomir Blaskic. Did you receive this document? Because it was forwarded to all units in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Are you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if this is the original signature -- but I don't think this is Blaskic's signature. I have a vague recollection of receiving that order, but I really can't remember the precise details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, would it be correct to say that under item 2, line 3 there is an order according to which all Muslims in HVO units are to be disarmed and isolated?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, not that all Muslims should be disarmed but that Muslims who don't obey orders are to be disarmed. That's what it says. Not all of them, only those who don't obey orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 4, are you ordered to control the traffic and transport of Muslims with equipment and weapons and such equipment and weapons should be confiscated and placed at the disposal of the HVO forces? Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it says that forces from the Jure Francetic Zenica Brigade and the Subic Zrinski Busovaca units should check the routes. But I wasn't ordered to confiscate anything. This wasn't my right. This is a new line. It says: "The 4th Battalion of the military police."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness can remember this order and the contents of the order, I would like this document to be admitted into evidence and I would like it to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number -- But yes, Mr. Withopf, you wanted to say something. It will still be marked for identification though. Mr. Withopf, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: If it's only for the purpose of marking it for identification, I wouldn't object. If it's for the purpose to tender it, I would certainly object, since I can't see the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have it marked for identification, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH45, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH45. But we have B/C/S and English versions, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The English translation will get the exhibit number DH45/E, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown document -- I think it's 099 through 93 dated the 16th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, is this an order that you issued?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, I would like to point out that in the course of our investigations we found this order among documents used in the Kordic case. Mr. Totic, would it be correct to say that as a brigade commander on the 16th of January, 1993 you refer to an order from the HVO Main Staff in Mostar, number 0166 through 93, dated the 15th of January - I showed it to you a minute ago - and also to an order from the command if the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, number 011-184/93, dated the 16th of January, 1993? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I referred to the order by the commander of the operative zone, which is based on the order from the Main Staff, which I didn't have at the time, because the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 2 in this order, line 3, is it correct to say that you requested that all the Muslims in brigade units of the HVO who do not respect --

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The witness has been asked to repeat the answer. Obviously it was not possible to translate it for the transcript. So can the witness please be asked the question again and he may please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please ask the witness the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, is it correct that in this order you refer to an order issued by the HVO Main Staff in 01-66/93 dated the 16th of January, 1993? I've already shown this to you. And you also refer to an order from the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, 01-185 through 93, dated the 16th of January, 1993? Are -- you recognised this a minute ago. Is that -- are those the orders you referred to? Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I referred to those two orders. But I never saw orders from the Main Staff. It's based on orders from the -- the orders from the command of that zone is based on those orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Totic, is it correct to say that in this order you're ordering your units - that's item 2, line 3 - that all Muslims in units of HVO brigades who fail to obey our orders should be disarmed, isolated, and you should be immediately informed of it?

utterances.speaker: ZIVKO TOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That concerns those who fail to obey orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that under item 3 you order the battalion commanders to organise supervision of all the movements by Muslim forces and especially -- can you please put the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have the time? There is a hearing after ours, so we're going to face a problem. Is there -- Mr. Registrar, is there something that should take place in this courtroom? Yes, it seems there is the Strugar case in the same courtroom. We are, therefore, obliged to stop here, to adjourn at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just going to kindly ask before we adjourn to have an exhibit number given to the last document. I want to avoid any confusions when we continue our cross-examination. Can we have an identification number for the document that the witness recognised as the one produced by himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly. If it's only for the purpose of an identification number, we don't object. If it's for the purpose of tendering it into evidence, we would object at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the purpose of identification, can you give us a number for the order that was signed by the witness on the 16th of January, 1993, Mr. Registrar. Can we have an identification number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be DH46, marked for identification for the B/C/S version; and DH46/E, marked for identification for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH46/E for English and DH46 for B/C/S. We have another problem, Madam Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has just suggested that the document produced in October should also be marked for identification. This is the document dated 24 October. This hasn't been done so far. So before we adjourn, can this document, dated 24th October, be also given an identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the document produced on the 24th of October, what document is that? What document are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has drawn my attention to the fact that the document dated 14 January has not been given an identification number. I apologise. I have headphones -- I didn't hear well. So the document dated 14 January has not been given an ID number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. 14 January is the document signed by Mr. Coric -- so that was a document signed by Mr. Valentin Coric. Can we have an identification number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH47, marked for identification for the B/C/S version; and DH47/E, marked for identification for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have to continue on Monday from 14.15 on. Witness, unfortunately you're going to have to spend the weekend in The Hague and wait for Monday. You maybe would like to go home already; however, the circumstances are such that you will have to come back on Monday at 14.15. Please be in the Tribunal building as from -- for 2.00 in the afternoon. Is there anything else that is -- needs to be said?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We are going to adjourn. We are still waiting for the two submissions regarding the digging of trenches and cruel treatment. You have promised to the Trial Chamber that you're going to submit these submissions on Monday. There is no urgency. It may be on Tuesday or on Wednesday. But this is still pending. Mr. Withopf, do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very briefly. That's in respect to the witness schedule for next week, and for that purpose can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we are going to ask you to leave the courtroom and return on Monday. The usher is going to show you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are moving into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 23rd day of February, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.56 p.m.,
